description:
Build a garden room at the bottom of the garden to be used for relaxation and writing. 
A (4m x 2.5m) garden room at 2.5m tall provides a generous 20 square meters of floor space. The strict 2.5 m height limit means the design will use a flat or pent roof (sloping 1-2 degrees for drainage) to ensure it complies with UK Permitted Development rules if built within 2m of a property boundary 
1. Foundation & Sub-base :Ground Screws: , to avoid deep concrete digging and keep the profile low.Air Gap: Ensure a minimum 50mm air gap beneath the floor joists to prevent wood rot and moisture buildup.
2. Floor StructureJoists: C24 grade timber 47mm x 100mm) spaced at 400mm centers to handle heavy furniture. Insulation: 190mm Rigid PIR foam (e.g., Celotex or Kingspan) fitted tightly between joists.Subfloor: 18mm OSB or Moisture-resistant tongue-and-groove chipboard.
3. Wall Framing & CladdingStuds: C24 (47mm x 100mm studs at (400mm centers. Wall Height: Keep the stud frame at approximately 2.1m tall. This leaves room for the roof joists, insulation, and cladding to stay under the (2.5m peak.Vapour Barrier: Breather membrane on the exterior, followed by vertical timber battens (for an air gap), and western red cedar cladding Internal Lining: Vapour control layer (VCL), service cavity for wiring, and (12.5mm plasterboard.
4. Roof Structure & Height BreakdownTo stay under (2.5m total external height:Joists: C24 (47mm x 150mm timber with a slight slope for drainage.Insulation: \(100mm PIR board, leaving a (50mm cross-ventilation gap.Roofing: (18mm OSB roof deck topped with EPDM rubber or GRP (fibreglass) for a watertight seal.Internal Ceiling: (50mm) insulated plasterboard or standard plasterboard fixed to the underside of joists.5. Glazing & Layout TipsDoors: A (3m wide set of aluminium bi-fold or uPVC French doors on the \(4m front aspect to flood the deep room with light. Small 1m x 150mm narrow windows on sides at 1.8m from floor.
